corrections_to_slate.claim: DreamOn's advertised mask_expansion/delete_eos_token kwargs are inert, so its headline length-elasticity was never exercised
corrections_to_slate.verdict: the mechanical fact is TRUE; the inference is REFUTED; the word 'advertised' is FALSE
corrections_to_slate.evidence: (1) both names appear 0 times in DreamOn generation_utils.py (sha256 9ef97ad61d77cfbe...); cfg.update(**both) returns them as unused and hasattr stays False. (2) BUT expansion is token-driven, not flag-gated: sampler tests x[0]==expand_token_id and ==delete_token_id, there is no 'if generation_config.mask_expansion' anywhere; config.json ships expand_token_id 151667 and mask_token_id 151666, and expand_budget=None becomes max_gen_len*2. (3) Our own telemetry proves it ran: dreamon_fim changed the output length on 871/1033 = 84.3% of tasks (803 longer, 68 shorter) from a constant 4 initial masks. (4) DreamOn's README Parameters section never documents either kwarg.
corrections_to_slate.consequence: Claim (b) is DEAD as a finding about DreamOn. It must NOT be published as a functional defect in a public model. What remains is an internal lab-notebook correction: OUR harness passed two no-op kwargs, and any of our wording claiming 'with mask_expansion=True' must be retracted (DLLM_RESULTS_20260807.md already does).

corrections_to_slate.claim: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B is a true matched lineage for Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B, differing only in mask_token_id

The six architectural fields are indeed identical across Qwen2.5-Coder-7B / Dream-Coder-Base / Dream-Coder-Instruct / DreamOn (hidden 3584, 28 layers, 28 heads, 4 KV heads, intermediate 18944, vocab 152064, rope_theta 1e6), verified from config.json on disk. robust_findings_that_survive: Suffix visibility is worth +0.2314 (AR) and +0.2991 (diffusion), both p<1e-56; bidirectional context is an affordance of the FIM task FRAMING, available to AR, not a property of the model class. This is the most defensible result in the pilot.
AR beats the two non-oracle-equivalent diffusion arms by 5-6pp (p<=1.9e-09), and this survives ceiling restriction (p<=3.7e-06).
The oracle length handout is worth +5.7pp to DreamOn (p=4.1e-14), so which diffusion configuration is the comparator decides whether AR 'wins'.
Zero generation errors and a passing grader self-test in all six arms; merge asserted 8/8 shards and no duplicate ids.

That suggestion was examined and REJECTED: A01 is a null-calibration protocol (input-blind nulls / best-constant floors / permutation tests) and this finding contains no null. subclaim_S4_inherited_from_A05.statement: On full-program code generation, DreamOn-v0-7B's reported weakness is substantially an artefact of one sampler-config integer: initial_masks 8->32 (all else frozen) moves MBPP+ .0899->.3545 (+26.5 pp) and HE+ .1280->.2561. subclaim_S4_inherited_from_A05.must_not_claim_1: NOT 'two independent artefacts each larger than typical method deltas'. The stitch defect's severity is CREATED by fixing the canvas: +0.61 pp at canvas=8, +4.27 pp at 32, +31.10 pp at 128. At the published operating point (initial_masks=8) only 1 of 164 raw outputs is multi-line, so the double-indent corrupts almost nothing and costs exactly 1 item (HumanEval/13). It is an INTERACTION, not a second standalone 31 pp defect.
subclaim_S4_inherited_from_A05.must_not_claim_2: NOT 'published numbers across the repo are affected, including the AR control'. Measured NIL blast radius: 17 arms re-graded, 2 move (both already-known DreamOn HE+ arms, +0.61 pp). All others have exactly 0 items on the buggy branch. There is no shared stitch, hence no diffusion-vs-AR asymmetry to claim.

base_axis_root_cause.items: every line L0-L10 of HumanEval/32 (entry_point find_zero); it is the split's ONLY find_zero task, which is exactly why the diff is 11 rows
base_axis_root_cause.mechanism: EVALPLUS VERSION. PyPI evalplus 0.3.1's find_zero special-oracle branch in eval/__init__.py:unsafe_execute does `assert abs(_poly(*inp,out))<=atol; continue` WITHOUT first setting details[i]=True / progress.value+=1. progress.value stays 0, untrusted_check returns details=[], and its own guard `if len(details)!=len(inputs): stat=FAIL` rewrites a genuine PASS into FAIL. The repo's vendored evalplus (upstream commit 26d6d00) carries the two missing lines before its continue.
base_axis_root_cause.deterministic: 3 repeats per version give identical results -- NOT host load, NOT wall-clock jitter

plus_axis_root_cause.mechanism: SANDBOX 4 GiB RLIMIT_AS, HOST-dependent and NOT a version difference. evalplus query_maximum_memory_bytes() defaults to 4 GiB and reliability_guard() applies it as RLIMIT_AS/RLIMIT_DATA inside the grading subprocess. These tasks' plus_input contains n ~ 1e6 whose reference outputs are ~1e6-element lists; materialising them exceeds 4 GiB of address space once the interpreter's own footprint counts. The bare MemoryError is swallowed by unsafe_execute's `except BaseException` and booked as a WRONG ANSWER rather than an error.

g0_verdict.condition_verbatim: KILL if an existing paper already shows a mask-diffusion LM's full-program code score is dominated by its initial-canvas budget -> S4 is a reproduction, citable as caveat only.
g0_verdict.verdict: THAT BRANCH FIRES. S4 is PREEMPTED.
preempting_papers: DAEDAL, arXiv:2508.00819v2 (2025-08-01), 'Beyond Fixed: Training-Free Variable-Length Denoising for Diffusion Large Language Models', Li/Dong/Zang/Cao/Wang/Lin. Venue: CoRR/arXiv-only per DBLP (CoRR 2025, DOI 10.48550/ARXIV.2508.00819); arXiv Comments field carries only a code URL, no acceptance note. Its Table 1 sweeps generation length 64..2048 on LLaDA-Instruct-8B with all else frozen: MBPP pass@1 20.8/28.0/37.4/38.2/37.4/38.8 and HUMANEVAL 18.9/26.2/36.0/47.0/47.6/47.0. That is MBPP +16.6 pp and HumanEval +28.7 pp from a canvas change alone, on full-program code -- the same phenomenon, direction and order of magnitude as S4's MBPP+ .0899->.3545 (+26.5 pp) / HE+ .1280->.2561. Paper's own words: 'For the baseline models, performance is highly dependent on manually tuning the generation length for each specific task.'

rho-EOS, arXiv:2601.22527v2 (2026-01-30), 'rho-EOS: Training-free Bidirectional Variable-Length Control for Masked Diffusion LLMs'. Venue: CoRR/arXiv-only per DBLP (CoRR 2026, DOI 10.48550/ARXIV.2601.22527). Independent replication on two more checkpoints: Tables 1-2 fixed-length baseline ladders give MBPP 21.0->36.7 (64->256) on LLaDA-Instruct-8B and 21.2->39.2 on LLaDA-1.5-8B.
supporting_not_decisive: dLLM-Var, arXiv:2510.24605 (2025-10-28), DBLP CoRR 2025. Table 2 pure-diffusion MBPP ladder 64->38.40, 128->42.00, 256->42.00, 512->43.20, 1024->41.80: right mechanism, only ~+4.8 pp, so magnitude does not match S4.

arXiv:2606.19475v2 (2026-06-17), 'Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis', Bertolani/Bucciarelli/Zini/Cornia/Baraldi, DBLP CoRR 2026. States S4's generalised framing as a headline: 'the behavior of DLMs is strongly influenced by generation-time design choices', and isolates the variable -- 'it is the generation length rather than the step count that drives performance degradation' -- with Dream/LLaDA MBPP+HumanEval curves that 'saturate or decline beyond 256-512 tokens'. Scales steps and length jointly (1:1) rather than freezing all else, and never touches EvalPlus (EvalPlus/canvas/initial-mask counts all 0), so it does not reproduce S4's exact contrast.
g0_verdict.concurrency_clause_does_not_apply: DAEDAL predates S4's 2026-08-12 statement by ~12.5 months and rho-EOS by ~6.5 months. Both are far outside the 2-3 month concurrency window, so neither can be set aside as concurrent work.
g0_verdict.why_this_was_not_already_obvious: DreamOn (arXiv:2602.01326) itself sweeps initial mask length (12 mentions, lengths 4-64, plus an oracle-length column) -- but ONLY on INFILLING. Its full text has MBPP=0, MBPP+=0, EvalPlus=0, HumanEval+=0 occurrences. So the canvas-sensitivity-on-infilling leg was already B10's own territory and did NOT preempt S4's full-program leg. What kills S4 is the LLaDA-family full-program literature (DAEDAL, rho-EOS), which is on a different model family and was not in B10's RELATED_WORK.md.
g0_verdict.adjacent_but_not_preempting: 15+ papers classed adjacent, each differing in the axis or the knob S4 turns on: DreamOn 2602.01326, CAL 2602.00476, LR-DLLM 2602.07546 (all infilling, not full-program); Evaluation Illusion 2606.29228 (dominant variable is prompt template x126, its length finding is on GSM8K, its code tables vary decoding method not canvas); CaRE 2607.24763 / 2606.12232 (cost unit + remasking strategy); ParallelBench 2510.04767 (parallel decoding); HLP 2410.03103 and Flexible-length Infilling 2506.13579 (both EMNLP 2025 Main, infilling); Template Infilling 2510.13870 and DIA 2606.04535 (both ACL 2026 Long, conditioning strategy); iLLaDA 2606.25331, DID 2603.23507, AR-vs-MDLM 2603.22075, PCD 2608.09424 (architecture/objective); and the weak-baseline genre 1907.06902 / 2407.07218 / 2204.03954 / 2505.09364 (establishes the species of result, none about diffusion LMs or code). Bar applied was 'already shows the same thing', not 'is in the same area', per memory/prior-work-differentiate-dont-abandon.md.
g0_verdict.authorities_reached: arXiv API (HTTPS only -- plain http timed out) ~20 structured queries plus id_list metadata pulls; arXiv HTML full text for 7 papers, so tables were read rather than abstracts trusted; DBLP publ API (flaky: long queries return total 0 or HTTP 500, short queries work) -- authoritative for the ACL-family hits; ACL Anthology per-paper pages (its /search/ endpoint is a JS Google-CSE shell that returns nothing to curl, so DBLP found candidates and Anthology verified them).
g0_verdict.authorities_that_refused: Semantic Scholar graph API: HTTP 429 on EVERY attempt, both /paper/search and /paper/arXiv:<id>, under a 20s/45s/90s/+30s backoff ladder; even a 1-token control query (query=test&limit=1) returned 429. This is the SAME blocker that stalled G0 on 2026-08-12, reproduced -- which is why multiple independent routes were used instead of treating one API's rate limit as evidence of absence. No S2 field is used anywhere in the verdict.
